To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a novel Bayesian analysis procedure to resolve the spatial-temporal organization in the plasma membrane of live cells and applied this method to study the effects of amyloid fibril formation in the membrane of live cells.

we developed a Bayesian analysis procedure for imaging fluorescence correlation spectroscopy data that allows us to visualize the temporal evolution of membrane domains in live cells, and we used it to show that hIAPP aggregates associate with the plasma membrane in a carpet-like manner.
the Bayesian analysis of imaging FCS enables the visualization of hIAPP-induced spatial organization of cellular plasma membrane domains and the temporal dynamics of their formation and disassembly.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spatial-temporal organization and dynamics of plasma membrane lipid domains and their interaction with amyloidogenic proteins in live cells.
the development of a new method to analyze the spatial and temporal evolution of the plasma membrane in live cells using total internal reflection fluorescence spectroscopy.
the development of new analytical methods and their application to study the interaction of amyloidogenic proteins with biological membranes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presented Bayesian analysis procedure, in conjunction with ITIR-FCS, provides a powerful and general approach for the investigation of the spatiotemporal organization of biological membranes, which has broad applicability to the study of the molecular mechanism underlying membrane-related diseases and biological processes.

hIAPP monomers and oligomers interact with the plasma membrane to induce the formation of membrane microdomains, which are characterized by increased density of lipids and decreased membrane fluidity.

hIAPP-induced membrane microdomain formation is a dynamic process with a spatially and temporally heterogeneous nature, and the membrane domain organization and dynamics are strongly dependent on the concentration of hIAPP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that hIAPP aggregates induce the formation of dense membrane microdomains in live cells.

a new analysis method has been developed to resolve the temporal evolution of spatially heterogeneous membrane domains in live cells, and that the method has been applied to resolve the temporal and spatial organization of plasma membrane microdomains induced by the cytotoxic hIAPP aggregates.
we developed an advanced analysis method for ITIR-FCS to reveal the spatial organization and temporal evolution of cellular plasma membrane domain organization induced by the toxic hIAPP aggregates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Bayesian analysis procedure provides a general approach to resolve the heterogeneous spatial-temporally organization of biological membrane system.
the Bayesian analysis procedure provides the ability to extract spatially resolved information on the temporal evolution of membrane microdomains in live cells.
the Bayesian analysis procedure can be used to resolve multiple diffusing species from a single ITIR-FCS dataset, which is not possible using the conventional approach.
